title: SEO in 2026 and its direct impact on SEO services

body:
SEO in 2026 and its direct impact on SEO services, written for companies buying or evaluating optimisation services who want to know what has changed from the standard offer of three years ago: "keywords, monthly articles, links, ranking report". Part of that model no longer works, part has become a minimum requirement, and a few new things (presence in generated answers, the brand entity, website-level quality) determine results. This article describes the changes, what agencies that understand them do differently, including us, and the list of questions to ask about any proposal.

The perspective is that of an agency in Alba Iulia working with small and medium-sized companies in Romania; the figures come from clients' accounts and our own website.

SEO in 2026 and its direct impact on SEO services

What has changed in search

  • Generated answers (AI Overviews, AI Mode) take clicks away from informational questions; the cited sources are few and chosen for clarity and trust. The effect is covered in the article on AI Mode and organic traffic.
  • Quality is assessed at website level: the proportion of useful pages matters; generic content in volume drags down good pages too.
  • The brand entity (who you are, confirmed by external sources) determines both rankings and recommendations from assistants.
  • Local has grown in importance: the Google Business profile and reviews bring customers directly to any business with a location.
  • Technical work has become basic hygiene: mandatory, but not an advantage in itself.
  • The 2024 spam policies eliminated shortcuts that still worked (scaled content, purchased links, expired domains).

What has disappeared from serious proposals

The old offerWhy it no longer worksWhat replaced it
"Guaranteed position 1"was never possible; in 2026, position no longer means a clickgoals for commercial traffic, enquiries and mentions
"10 articles a month"generic volume lowers the website's assessment2-4 pages a month, with experience and your own data, plus consolidation of old pages
"50 links a month"purchased links are targeted by spam updatesa few earned links and mentions from relevant sources
"Ranking report"rankings no longer reflect traffica report on non-branded clicks, conversions, page groups and AI presence
"On-page optimisation" as a deliverableit is a requirement, not a resultincluded in the audit and maintenance

What an SEO service looks like in 2026

1. The audit, with priorities

Technical (indexing, speed, duplicates), content (what pages exist, what is missing, what needs consolidating), trust (identity, authors, reviews, mentions), local, and access for AI bots. The deliverable is a list ordered by impact, not an 80-page report; what ours contains is on the SEO auditpage.

2. Commercial pages first

Services, categories, products: with process, prices or benchmarks, who they are for, evidence, and answers to real questions; these are the pages that withstand generated answers and are cited when the user asks for a provider. On our own website, we rewrote the home page and service pages with the process over 3, 6 and 12 months and real reviews, after the data showed that almost all query-page pairs with clicks were commercial.

3. Content with experience, less and better

Articles answering clients' questions with figures, cases and our own angles; consolidation of paired articles and expansion of thin ones (we did both on our blog, with 54 articles expanded and 13 redirected in two days); real authors; sources. The structure cited in answers is covered in the article on adapting content for AI Overviews.

4. The entity and mentions

About the company, authors, structured data, aligned profiles, real Google reviews, and mentions in industry sources; the plan is in the article on Generative Engine Optimization.

5. Local, for businesses with a location

A Google Business profile maintained monthly, with reviews and replies; genuine local pages; our local SEO service is built around this routine.

6. Honest measurement

Non-branded clicks by page group, comparisons over equal periods and against the previous year, organic conversions, brand presence in assistants for a fixed set of questions, and branded queries (a sign of authority). The monthly report says what was done, what changed in the figures, and what comes next, in two pages.

What to ask for in any proposal

  1. What exactly is delivered in the first month and in the sixth month (pages, not "optimisation").
  2. How links are obtained; "we have partnerships" without names means their own networks or purchasing.
  3. Who writes the content, with what data, and who checks it; if AI is used, how it is checked.
  4. What metrics are in the report and why; ask for non-branded clicks and conversions, not rankings.
  5. What happens during a Google update: how it is measured and who decides what changes.
  6. Access: the Search Console property and Analytics remain the company's; the agency gets user access, not ownership.
  7. What the agency does not do (guarantees, price discounts with "links included"); a clear refusal is a good sign.

How to evaluate results, and when

  • Months 1-2: technical issues fixed (indexing, speed), commercial pages rewritten; an effect on impressions in Search Console.
  • Months 3-6: initial increases in non-branded clicks and enquiries; rankings on pages 1-2 for the main commercial phrases.
  • Months 6-12: stable rankings, growth in branded queries, presence in AI answers to commercial questions.
  • Warning signs: a report with rankings only, traffic growing only for the brand, generic articles in volume, and links from unknown websites in Search Console's links report.

An example of a contract in 2026

A technical services company with an old website and a previous agency that had delivered "8 articles and 30 links a month" for two years, without growth. The audit showed: 190 generic articles on subjects unrelated to the services, a link profile with 400 domains from directories and blogs for hire, 200-word service pages without prices, and an incomplete Google Business profile. The new six-month contract: consolidating 190 articles into 40, with redirects; rewriting the five service pages with process and prices; the Google Business profile and reviews; two articles a month with cases from the business; disavowing the obvious network and ten real mentions from associations and local press. At six months: non-branded clicks 70% above the baseline, requests for quotes doubled, and the website cited by two AI assistants for the question "who provides service X in county Y". Less content, fewer links, more results.

How an agency's team changes

The service in 2026 requires different skills from that of 2020: data analysis (Search Console, logs, page groups), writing with industry experience (not generic writers), understanding generated answers and entities, solid technical skills (indexing, speed, security), and, increasingly, scripts and language models used for volume and verification, with humans making decisions. Agencies still using "writers paid per article and bundled links" deliver exactly what no longer works; ask who actually works on your account and what they have done in the past year.

Indicative prices

For small companies in Romania, a serious monthly service (initial audit, 2-4 pages a month, technical maintenance, local, report) costs between 300 and 900 euros a month, depending on competition and volume; a separate audit, 300-900 euros. Below 200 euros a month there is no room for real work; above 1.500 is justified for large shops or competitive national markets. Our benchmarks are public on the SEO optimisation pricespage, precisely because an offer without a price loses customers who compare.

What has not changed

Patience: lasting results come in 6-12 months; useful, people-first content wins with every update; earned links remain the strongest signal after content; correct measurement separates what works from what does not. The complete guide we give clients is on the website, in 12 chapters; the basic principles are in the article on what SEO is, and growth strategies in the article on increasing organic traffic.

Frequently asked questions

  1. Does SEO still make sense with AI Overviews? Yes, with an emphasis on commercial content and being the cited source; generic informational content no longer makes sense.
  2. Can I do SEO myself? Yes, with 4-8 hours a month and the guides on the website; an agency brings speed, experience across cases, and time.
  3. How do I know whether the agency uses prohibited methods? Ask directly about links and content; check Search Console's links report and branded queries versus the rest.
  4. What happens if I stop the service? Organic results remain for a while (unlike advertising), but erode without maintenance and new content.
